name: ReactUse

hlido_opinion.headline: Mature, well-documented React hooks library (110+ hooks, TypeScript-first, SSR-safe) with a real MCP server so coding agents can query it — a solid developer utility whose 'agent' relevance is as a component, not an autonomous product.
hlido_opinion.body: ReactUse is a large, VueUse-inspired collection of production-oriented React hooks — the documentation lays out 110+ of them, organised into clear buckets (state, effect, element, browser, sensors), and the library advertises tree-shaking, SSR-safety and a TypeScript-first API. The surface is that of a settled open-source utility rather than a launch: an ordered hook index, a changelog, a blog, and adoption claims (Shopee, PDD, Ctrip) that read as credible for a library at 1k+ stars. What makes it relevant to an agentic register at all is that it ships an MCP server (the repo carries an MCP top-list badge and the `mcp` topic), which lets a coding agent look up and reason about the hooks programmatically. That is a legitimate but narrow kind of agent-relevance: ReactUse is a dependency a developer or a coding agent uses, not an agent that does work on its own. Judged as what it is — a developer library with an agent-readable surface — it is dependable and clearly presented. The caveats are the usual ones for this class: real quality lives in tree-shaking correctness, SSR edge-cases and per-hook stability, none of which a public-surface review exercises, and the adoption logos are asserted rather than independently confirmed here.

tier_rationale: STEADY (74): the documentation is thorough and well-structured, the API surface is large and specific, open-source with visible maintenance (changelog, blog), and it exposes an MCP server that makes it genuinely queryable by coding agents. Not higher because agent-relevance is component-level (a library, not an autonomous agent), per-hook correctness/SSR behaviour is untested at Tier-1, and the enterprise-adoption claims are unverified.
what_it_does_well: Large, well-organised hook catalogue (110+) with a clear category index
TypeScript-first, tree-shakable and SSR-safe by design
Ships an MCP server so coding agents can discover and use the hooks programmatically
Signs of active maintenance — changelog, blog, ordered docs
Familiar mental model for anyone who knows VueUse
what_it_fails_at: It is a component library, not an autonomous agent — 'agent' relevance is indirect
Per-hook correctness, tree-shaking and SSR edge behaviour are untested at Tier-1
Enterprise adoption claims (Shopee/PDD/Ctrip) are asserted, not independently verified here
No standalone runtime to behaviourally exercise as an agent
best_for: React/TypeScript teams wanting a broad, maintained hooks toolkit
Coding agents that can consume the MCP server to look up and apply hooks
Projects that need SSR-safe, tree-shakable utilities out of the box
Developers already comfortable with the VueUse pattern
not_recommended_for: Buyers looking for an autonomous agent or end-user product
Teams that need an independently benchmarked performance guarantee before adopting

evidence_urls.claim: Exposes an MCP server (mcp topic + MCP top-list badge)
Used in production by Shopee, PDD and Ctrip

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: A React hooks library consumed as a dependency; its MCP server lets a coding agent discover and apply hooks. Agent-relevance is component-level (something an agent uses), not an autonomous agent to drive.

checklist.evidence: '110+ Essential React Hooks Library for TypeScript'
Open-source library, free; 'Buy me a coffee'/sponsor links
Full hook index and docs shown on site
